Article Title: 'Targeting civilian infrastructure unacceptable': India condemns Houthis attack on Riyadh airports
Article Text:
Houthi group attacked Saudi airports. (ANI)

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Thursday condemned recent attacks on two airports in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh by Yemen's Iran-linked Houthi group, calling the targeting of civilian infrastructure “completely unacceptable”.MEA issued a statement saying that the attacks on Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh had resulted in civilian deaths and injuries.“India condemns the attacks over the past few days targeting Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which have resulted in civilian deaths and injuries,” the MEA said.“The targeting of civilian infrastructure is completely unacceptable. We express our deepest condolences to the families of those who have lost their loved ones. We wish speedy recovery for those injured. We express solidarity and stand with the people and government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” it added.Three people were killed and 36 injured in attacks on the two Saudi airports over two days, according to Saudi authorities cited by the BBC.Two people were killed and 28 wounded in an attack on Abha International Airport, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said on Wednesday.In a separate attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, one person was killed and eight others were injured, it said. The attacks took place on October 6 and 7, although GACA did not specify which airport was targeted on each day.Two women, who were Moroccan and Algerian nationals, were among those killed in the Abha attack, according to GACA.The attacks, for which the Houthis have claimed responsibility, mark an escalation in the renewed fighting between Saudi-backed government forces and the Iran-aligned Houthi group in Yemen.Saudi Arabia’s civil aviation authority did not identify those responsible for the attacks. However, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had targeted both Saudi airports with ballistic missiles and drones.Saree also claimed that the Houthis attacked Aden International Airport in Yemen on Wednesday. The airport is a major international gateway for areas of Yemen outside Houthi control and has been targeted during previous bouts of fighting.He said the attacks on the Saudi airports were carried out in “response to the Saudi aggression against our country”, which he claimed involved “60 airstrikes and missile attacks in the past 24 hours”.Earlier in the day, the Houthi group also issued a “last warning” to global airlines operating flights through Saudi airspace, saying the area had become a “theater for our military operations”.The group also claimed it had attacked King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with a ballistic missile. There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia of the latest claim.Saree said the missile “struck its target with precision and caused the disruption of airport operations.”“We reiterate our call and warning "for the last time" to all global airlines regarding the consequences of continuing to operate flights in Saudi airspace, which has become a theater for our military operations,” Saree said.He added that airspace over the “sacred areas” in Mecca and Medina was exempt from the warning. The Houthi warning came amid heightened concerns over attacks on Saudi airports and airspace.The US Mission in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday urged American citizens to exercise heightened vigilance amid Houthi threats. It warned that the situation could lead to flight cancellations, airspace closures and other travel disruptions.
Article Summary: Houthi group attacked saudi airports. Mea issued a statement saying that the attacks on abha international airport and king khalid international airport in riyadh had resulted in civilian deaths and injuries. Three people were killed and 36 injured in attacks on the two saudi airports over two days, according to saudi authorities.

Article Title: WHO puts stroke, cancer, mental health on 10-year traditional medicine research agenda
Article Text:
The World Health Organization has set forth a comprehensive research agenda for the upcoming decade, focusing on pivotal health conditions such as stroke, mental health, cancer, and reproductive health.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From stroke and cancer to mental health and pain management, the World Health Organization has identified major health conditions for research into traditional, complementary and integrative medicine over the next decade.Its 2025-2034 research agenda identifies stroke, mental health, pain management, musculoskeletal conditions, cancer, metabolic and endocrine disorders, and reproductive health and childbirth as priority areas. Prevention and health promotion, healthy ageing and healthy childhood are also included.The report highlights a striking mismatch between disease burden and research. Stroke ranks third globally in causes of mortality and disability, yet less than 1% of traditional, complementary and integrative medicine-funded grants address the condition. Mental health ranks eighth among contributors to disability-adjusted life years, but the review found very few or no grants specifically focused on mental health conditions. Musculoskeletal conditions are also a prominent cause of disability globally but remain under-researched relative to their burden.Cancer, too, features among the priority areas, with the report noting rising global incidence and calling for research into integrative oncology and palliative care.For metabolic health and endocrine disorders, WHO identifies the need for stronger evidence, including longer-term studies on conditions such as type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome.WHO says the aim is to generate stronger evidence on effectiveness, safety, regulation and health-system integration so countries can make informed decisions about the role of these approaches in healthcareThe research agenda also puts patient safety under the spotlight. It calls for studies on herb-drug interactions, monitoring and reporting of adverse events, regulatory and quality-assurance systems, and the safe integration of traditional, complementary and integrative medicine into primary healthcare.The push comes against a broader funding gap. WHO says traditional, complementary and integrative medicine is widely used globally, with use reaching up to 80% of populations in some settings, while less than 1% of global health research funding is directed towards research in the field.India has a direct connection to the agenda. The WHO report acknowledges financial support from the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, for its development and publication. India was also among the health ministries that participated in the Second WHO Global Summit on Traditional Medicine, held in New Delhi in December 2025.The report, however, is a research-prioritisation framework rather than a clinical guideline or recommendation to use any particular traditional medicine.
Article Summary: The world health organization has set forth a comprehensive research agenda for the upcoming decade. The 2025-2034 research agenda identifies stroke, mental health, pain management, musculoskeletal conditions, cancer, metabolic and endocrine disorders, and reproductive health and childbirth.

Article Title: Rupee may be undervalued, markets can be irrational: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra
Article Text:
File photo: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra

Sensex snaps winning run

MUMBAI: Reserve Bank of India governor Sanjay Malhotra said the rupee was undervalued and the central bank would intervene to ensure orderly movement in the currency market even as it closed at 96.78 on Wednesday, down 36 paise from its previous close, after falling to a five-month low of 96.85 during the day."By a number of estimates, including the real effective exchange rate, the rupee is not overvalued. It may be undervalued," Malhotra said at a press conference after the MPC meeting. He was responding to a question on whether the rupee market was irrational."Markets can be quite irrational in the short run. It's only in the long run that they are able to find the right value," he said.The governor said RBI would support the rupee's orderly movement and help it find its "correct value", while ensuring there was no excessive volatility.Malhotra also said a correction in the valuation of global AI stocks could redirect foreign capital to emerging markets such as India. He said a correction in AI stocks would not have a major negative impact on India and "if at all, there may be" a positive impact.Malhotra said that US tariffs and the absence of a trade deal would be a negative but could be offset by a trade deal with other countries.Despite a robust services trade surplus and strong net remittance receipts, the current account deficit widened in July because of a higher merchandise trade deficit, Malhotra said.The merchandise trade deficit rose to $58.7 billion in July and Aug from $55.1 billion in the same period a year earlier, mainly because of higher imports of electronic goods and crude oil. On external financing, Malhotra said net FDI had shown sustained improvement, with inflows rising to $13.8 billion in the first four months of the year from $9.6 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier. The increase was driven by higher gross inflows and a slowdown in the growth of outward FDI."Robust gross FDI reflects the strong interest of global investors in India," he said. FPI recorded net outflows of $10.3 billion during the period up to Oct 5. However, capital-flow measures announced in the June policy had supported inflows, he said. The balance of payments is consequently expected to record a healthy surplus this year.Malhotra also clarified that the new trade rules are aimed at improving ease of business and do not impose a reporting burden on individuals who get paid from overseas for software or other services. Nor does it apply to individuals paying for software or some subscriptions. Small exporters can use a self-declaration for bills up to Rs 10 lakh; and banks, not exporters or importers, handle reporting on the RBI's system. The aim is to simplify trade procedures while improving RBI's data on services exports, he said.After a two-session gain, sensex slid on Wednesday after RBI hiked interest rates for the first time in over three-and-a-half years. Sensex closed 429 points down at 72,639 points while on NSE, Nifty closed 173 points down at 22,603 points.On BSE, two indices-PSU banks and housing finance-each closed nearly 1% up while two other indices-bankex and financial services-closed barely changed.
Article Summary: Rbi governor sanjay malhotra said the rupee was undervalued. He said the central bank would intervene to ensure orderly movement in the currency market. Sensex closed 429 points down at 72,639 points while on nse, nifty closed 173 points down.

Article Title: Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex tanks over 1,100 points; Nifty50 below 22,250 - top reasons for fall
Article Text:
Adding to the pressure on markets, Brent crude prices rose another 2%.

Why is stock market down today?

RBI’s policy stance change

US bond yields

soar to 24-year high

Oil jumps above $102/barrel

FIIs continue to sell

Fed rate hike worries

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex and Nifty50 , the Indian equity benchmarks, crashed in trade on Thursday, with both indices down around 1%. Investors reacted to the RBI’s policy tightening and repo rate hike, continued FII selling and other negative factors. BSE Sensex plunged over 1,000 points while NSE Nifty50 slipped below the 22,300 levels.At 1:25 PM, Nifty50 was trading at 22,260.70, down 342 points or 1.51%. BSE Sensex was at 71,670.06, down 968 points or 1.33%.. BSE Sensex was at 71,764.88, down 873.82 points or 1.20%. The sharp decline erased nearly Rs 10.93 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of companies listed on the BSE.ITC, Adani Ports, IndiGo, Power Grid and Reliance Industries (RIL) were among the biggest losers on the Sensex, with their shares declining as much as 4%. On the other hand, Titan and major IT stocks such as Tech Mahindra, HCL Technologies, TCS and Infosys gained up to 2%, providing some support to the benchmark index.The RBI delivered its first rate increase in nearly four years. However, market analysts viewed the central bank’s decision to move its policy stance from ‘neutral’ to ‘calibrated tightening’, against a difficult global geopolitical backdrop, as the more significant signal for markets.Jefferies expects the RBI to raise interest rates by around 100 basis points during the current tightening cycle.Nomura also pointed to the change in stance as an unexpected development. “We believe this was aimed at anchoring inflation expectations and building a buffer against adverse global conditions. However, the message was mixed, with the MPC clarifying that “calibrated tightening” only signalled “no rate cuts”, and indicated data dependence going forward,” it added.VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments Limited says that the calibrated tightening stance of the RBI has implications for markets.“With two more rate hikes of 25bp each likely in this rate hiking cycle, there will be pressure on valuations rising from higher fixed income returns. Investor preferences also might shift marginally towards interest inelastic segments like pharmaceuticals,” he says.The global selloff in bonds intensified, sending yields to their highest levels in several years. The US 30-year bond yield climbed above 5.71%, while the yield on benchmark 10-year notes rose past 5.3%. The two-year note yield also moved close to 4.9%.Rising bond yields generally make debt markets more appealing to investors, which can increase pressure on emerging-market equities. Since bond prices and yields move in opposite directions, a sharp rise in yields indicates significant selling in the bond market.Adding to the pressure on markets, Brent crude prices rose another 2% to move above $102 per barrel. Investors remained worried about the security of Middle East oil supplies as attacks on shipments increased in the Gulf and around the strategically important Strait of Hormuz.Tankers travelling through the Strait of Hormuz faced the highest number of attacks in a single week since the Iran war began earlier this year, even as Gulf producers raised exports. The increase in attacks came as crude shipments from the Gulf increased, but with greater risks and higher costs for cargoes and crews. On Wednesday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said a tanker north of Qatar had been hit by multiple projectiles, resulting in casualties.Meanwhile, US crude inventories fell by 3.2 million barrels last week to 424.1 million barrels, according to the Energy Information Administration on Wednesday. A Reuters poll of analysts had forecast a smaller decline of 1.7 million barrels.The record selling spree of FIIs continues, exacerbated by the rising bond yields. Foreign investors continued their selling spree in Indian equities on Wednesday, offloading shares worth more than Rs 6,121 crore on a net basis, according to provisional NSE data. Their net selling has now reached nearly Rs 57,000 crore across nine straight sessions through Wednesday.Since the start of September, FIIs have been net sellers in 20 of the 25 trading sessions. Their sustained selling, despite brief periods of buying, has continued to weigh on Dalal Street since the Middle East war began earlier this year.VK Vijayakumar notes that a distinct and strong trend in the market in recent months has been the increasing preference for growth stocks over value stocks.“Growth stocks are being accumulated at high valuations while value stocks are languishing at fair valuations. Sustained selling in large-caps by the FIIs have contributed significantly to this trend. With the US 10-year bond yield hovering above 5.3%, FIIs will continue to sell on every rally. This will put the Nifty large-caps under pressure for some more time,” he warns.“A reversal in this trend will happen only when FIIs turn buyers, and there is no clarity on when this will happen. In brief, this frustrating period in the market might continue for some more time. Remaining invested in value stocks will be rewarded in the long run. Investors should also look at the good opportunities in fixed income in this rising rate environment,” he adds.Minutes from the Federal Reserve's meeting showed a split among policymakers last month over the case for raising interest rates. Some officials believed a hike was needed to contain the effects of energy and other price shocks, while a more hawkish group saw higher rates as necessary to guard against emerging inflation driven by demand.Traders currently see only an 18% probability of a rate increase later this month, while the odds of a December hike are being priced at 80%, according to CME's FedWatch tool, as cited by Reuters.
Article Summary: Bse sensex plunged over 1,000 points while nse nifty50 slipped below the 22,300 levels. The sharp decline erased nearly rs 10.93 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of companies listed on the bse. Investors remained worried about the security of middle east oil supplies.

Article Title: 'We'll do it': PM Modi gives slogan for 2047 goals; credits people’s support for 25-year unbroken run
Article Text:
PM Modi said the Indian economy was considered a ‘gone case’ when he took office in 2014, and the picture has completely changed now

Target unprecedented and extraordinary goals: Modi

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi chose the milestone of his unbroken run of 25 years as head of govt on Wednesday to deliver a message imbued with optimism and passion for achieving the target of developed India by 2047, crediting people's support for his feat and asking citizens to join him in dedicating themselves to the ambitious goal."We will do it," Modi said at a BJP event, a clarion call which repeatedly punctuated his one-hour-long address and what, he said, has guided him in setting his goals, since he became Gujarat CM in 2001 with no administrative experience, and achieve them with support of "janshakti" (people's power)."Karma is my dharma. When I took oath as Gujarat CM, I never thought such an occasion will come," he said at Viksit Bharat Sankalp Sabha, asking people to take a pledge to put the nation first and not stop till India becomes a developed country. His speech came amid the opposition's high-decibel protest in the heart of the city over the SIR row but he appeared unfazed.Modi’s speech on his 25 years as head of govt came amid the opposition’s protest in Delhi over the SIR row, but he did not join the issue, except for a sideswipe at his rivals when he said a big tragedy for the country had been that it was divided for votes due to political expedience.Water crisis in agriculture or power shortage does not hit any particular caste or community, Modi said.“When a problem troubles everyone, then the solution too should cover everyone,” he said, adding this was why his govt linked good governance and saturation to inclusion.Reiteration of his “tireless” resolve to make India a leading player in a gamut of sectors, including tourism, education, sports, entertainment and science, ran through the nearly hour-long speech as its central theme.“Our pilot (Smit Machchhar) is being discussed globally today. Made-in-India planes will be discussed tomorrow... It will be an injustice to the country if we set small and easy goals. We should target unprecedented and extraordinary goals,” Modi said.“Viksit Bharat by 2047: we will do it. Top three economy: we will do it. Self-reliant: we will do it,” he said.Addressing the criticism that his target of “Viksit Bharat by 2047” is too far into the future, he said the idea of an independent India two decades before 1947 had looked improbable. India has 140 crore citizens now as against less than 40 crore then and is much more capable, he said.Modi said the Indian economy was considered a “gone case” when he took office in 2014, and the picture had completely changed now.Lauding RSS volunteers and BJP members, he recalled his rise from a humble background, saying he was always driven by a desire to learn. “No incident was a waste for me. Those who helped me win taught me humility. Those who brought me down taught me to stand up. Those who opposed me taught me the power of democracy. Every crisis was a test of my patience,” he said.Modi said he was never driven by ambition but mission, adding he never intended to contest elections and was busy helping others fight polls as a senior organisational functionary in BJP before being asked to take over as Gujarat CM.
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi chose the milestone of his unbroken run of 25 years as head of govt to deliver a message imbued with optimism and passion for achieving the target of developed india by 2047. "karma is my dharma. When i took oath as gujarat cm, i never thought such an occasion will come," he said at viksit bharat sankalp sabha.

Article Title: Pakistan's terror monsters now wreak havoc in its own backyard: India at UN
Article Text:
‘You cannot run with the hares’: India tears into Pakistan’s terror record at UN

Pakistan’s own leaders expose terror threat

'Circular economy of words'

Stronger international cooperation Action against terror networks Better intelligence sharing Stronger measures against terror financing 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: India used the UN stage to turn Pakistan’s own words against it, arguing that the terror networks Islamabad once nurtured have now come back to haunt their own backyard, a reality, New Delhi said, that even Pakistan’s leaders have begun to acknowledge. India also urged the international community to take stronger action against states accused of sponsoring terrorism.Speaking at the UN General Assembly’s Sixth Committee, which deals with legal affairs, India’s first secretary Raghoo Puri said Pakistan had long portrayed itself as both a victim and a frontline state in the fight against terrorism."Pakistan has presented itself as a frontline state in combating terrorism and as a victim, while masking the fact that the Frankenstein’s (monster) the Pakistani state has created and lost control over have moved from wreaking havoc in neighbouring countries to doing the same in Pakistan," Puri said on Wednesday."This was exposed recently by a provincial chief minister of Pakistan, and may I jog the memory of colleagues to an interview in 2018 by her father and former prime minister of Pakistan, exposing this dark secret," he said."You cannot run with the hares and hunt with the hounds," Puri warned. "Reality never works like that".Puri was responding to remarks by Pakistan’s deputy Permanent Representative Usman Jadoon, who had launched an attack on India during the committee proceedings.Puri pointed to recent remarks by Punjab chief minister Maryam Nawaz , who said her province faced a bigger threat from neighbouring Pakistani provinces than from neighbouring countries.Maryam Nawaz, who leads Pakistan’s Punjab province, said last month in Lahore: "Unfortunately, the threat Punjab, a province of 130 million, faces comes less from my neighbouring countries and more from my neighbouring provinces."Earlier this month, she also questioned the idea of distinguishing between different forms of extremist violence, saying anyone involved in terrorism should be treated as a terrorist regardless of their political motives.Puri also referred to an interview given by Maryam Nawaz’s father, former Pakistan prime minister Nawaz Sharif, to Dawn in 2018. Sharif had spoken about militant groups operating from Pakistan and questioned whether they should be allowed to cross the border and carry out attacks in India."Militant organisations are active. Call them non-state actors; should we allow them to cross the border and kill 150 people in Mumbai?" he had said.Puri did not name either Maryam Nawaz or Nawaz Sharif while making his remarks.Puri also hit back at Pakistan’s claims about the outcome of Operation Sindoor , India’s counterterror military action to the Pahalgam attack."If bombed-out airfields and cratered runways look like victory to Pakistan, they are, of course, welcome to enjoy it," he said.He accused Pakistan of continuing to spread false claims about the operation and said its approach was part of a wider campaign of disinformation.Puri said the "Pakistani representative’s desperation to falsely tout the Pakistani military’s narrative on the outcome of Operation Sindoor" was consistent with Pakistan’s long-running use of state-backed misinformation and psychological warfare.Puri also took a swipe at Pakistan after its delegation made a second intervention, repeating what he described as old arguments."Pakistan believes in the circular economy of words and narratives," Puri said."If this much effort had actually been made in countering terrorism rather than narrative building, misinformation, and disinformation, the world would have been a better place," he said."But nothing more can be expected from a Form 47 government," he added, referring to Pakistan’s political system and alleged manipulation of the electoral process.Puri also challenged Pakistan’s claims on minority rights and accused Islamabad of allowing religious extremism to flourish."The victims in Pahalgam were not asked about their political orientation; they were asked about their religion," Puri said."It is therefore deeply ironic that Pakistan speaks of combating religious hatred while allowing the conditions that enable it to persist and thrive, especially by fomenting cross-border terrorism," he added.Puri referred to the Pahalgam terror attack, in which terrorists targeted tourists after asking about their religion.He said the attack showed the consequences of allowing extremist groups and crossborder terrorism to continue.Puri also questioned Pakistan’s claims that it was taking action against Jaish-e-Mohammed chief Masood Azhar, who is listed by the UN as a terrorist.Pakistan had increased the reward for information leading to Azhar’s arrest from Pakistani rupees 50 lakh to 70 lakh."Pakistan glosses over its state support for terrorism by announcing enhanced rewards for apprehending UN-listed head of Jaish-e-Mohammed, terrorist and mastermind of several attacks against my country," Puri said."When the media can reach Masood Azhar and get confirmation from him about the success of Operation Sindoor, surely the Pakistani state knows his whereabouts," he said.Azhar had earlier appeared in a video in which he claimed that his family infrastructure had been destroyed during India’s strikes on Bahawalpur as part of Operation Sindoor.Puri also recalled Pakistan’s earlier claims that Jaish-e-Mohammed was no longer active."Just a few months ago, Pakistani representatives used this forum to call the Jaish-e-Mohammed a defunct organisation," Puri said. "The world has seen the script play earlier, and we are clear-eyed that this time also it is going to be no different."Puri warned that allowing terrorist groups to operate with political protection could undermine international efforts against terrorism."When terrorist groups are allowed to operate under state political power, international commitments become meaningless, and when perpetrators are provided safe havens, the victims of terrorism are denied justice," he said.He also cited the example of al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden, who was found in Abbottabad, Pakistan, years after the 9/11 attacks."The world has not forgotten 9/11, and where its perpetrators, including Osama bin Laden, were caught," Puri said.He then pointed to the 2008 Mumbai attacks."The world has not forgotten 26/11," when Pakistani terrorists killed 166 people in Mumbai, he said. "The world has not forgotten Pahalgam."Puri also referred to Pakistan’s record on terror financing and the upcoming meeting of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF)."The world is aware of Pakistan’s financial support to terrorism, as also, the FATF plenary meeting coming up soon," he said.The FATF, the global body that monitors terror financing and money laundering, is scheduled to hold its next plenary meeting in Paris from October 26 to 30.
Article Summary: 'you cannot run with the hares': india tears into pakistan’s terror record at un. India invokes 9/11, 26/11 and pahalgam and invokes pakistan's own leaders expose terror threat. ‘bombed-out airfields’ are not victory, india says. "pakistan believes in the circular economy of words and narratives," puri said.

NEW DELHI: There was a stark 73% decline in the “average size of monitored wildlife populations” globally over a 52-year period (1970-2022), whereas India became one of the most important countries that were successfully involved in wildlife recovery by turning around the populations of certain animals, including tigers, one-horned rhino and Ganga river dolphins, according to WWF’s biennial Living Planet Report (LPR) released on Thursday.Though the LPR remains silent on country-specific data, experts explaining certain points ahead of the release noted “significant changes” in biodiversity in India where nine species of mammals figured in the “critically endangered” list, 39% of 942 bird species reported “clear decline” and 32% (136 species) of the amphibians have been “threatened” by a combination of factors including agricultural practices and climate change.Nine mammals classified as critically endangered (CR) in India under International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) criteria are Kashmir Stag/Hangul, Malabar Large-spotted Civet, Chinese Pangolin, Andaman Shrew, Jenkin’s Shrew, Nicobar Shrew, Namdapha Flying Squirrel, Large Rock Rat and Leafletted Leaf-nosed Bat.The report is based on Living Planet Index (LPI), which tracks how species populations are faring around the world.The Index, produced by Zoological Society of London, includes 35,803 population trends of 5,790 vertebrate species (mammals, birds, amphibians, reptiles and fish) from 1970 to 2022.It noted the strongest decline in freshwater ecosystems (-85%), followed by terrestrial (-69%) and then marine (-59%) over the 1970 baseline. Region-wise, Latin America and the Caribbean registered the highest decline of 95%, followed by Africa (80%), Asia-Pacific (49%), North America (28%), and Europe and Central Asia (23%).The report said the “habitat loss and degradation” are the most frequently reported threat affecting monitored wildlife populations, followed by overexploitation, climate change, pollution, invasive species and disease. “These threats are, in turn, driven by broader systemic failures across the food, energy and finance systems,” it said.Although the overall trend is negative due to the magnitude of the declining trends, LPR noted that half of the populations included in the Index are “stable or increasing”. It highlighted recoveries in populations of green turtles, bluefin tuna, tigers and southern African elephants, which demonstrate that targeted conservation interventions can deliver proven results.Asked about the biggest takeaway in the LPR that flagged an upward trend in the numbers of species in India including tigers, Asiatic lion, common leopard and snow leopard, Sejal Worah, programme director, WWF-India, said one big message is that the country can actually turn around wildlife populations and species with the right combination of factors, including political will, required finances, civil society engagement and involvement with local communities. India has shown that wildlife recovery is possible, she added.WWF-India, during its pre-release presentation, however, underlined certain significant changes in biodiversity in India. It noted that the country is home to around 135 bat species that face neglect due to a “lack of research” and are threatened by urbanisation, deforestation, land-use changes and climate change. It also said that freshwater fish are among the most threatened vertebrates.“The LPR 2026 is both a stark reminder of the scale of the biodiversity crisis and a message of hope. While the LPI continues to highlight significant declines in monitored wildlife populations, the report also shows that these declines are not inevitable. Species recoveries, including those of tigers in India and globally, demonstrate what sustained conservation action, collaboration and long-term commitment can achieve,” said Ravi Singh, secretary general & CEO, WWF-India.Referring to data, the report said, “Although the overall global trend is negative, half (50%) of the populations included in the LPI are stable (7%) or increasing (43%). The magnitude of the declining trends, however, exceeds that of the increasing trends resulting in an average decline of 73% for the global LPI.”It, however, clarified that the percentage change in the index reflects the cumulative average proportional change in monitored animal population sizes at sites around the world since 1970, not the number of individual animals lost, nor the number of populations lost.It also said that the LPI are not directly comparable as they contain different sets of species (967 more populations and 295 more species have been added to the dataset since the LPR 2024) and cover a longer period each time.
Article Summary: There was a stark 73% decline in the “average size of monitored wildlife populations” globally over a 52-year period (1970-2022) india became one of the most important countries that were successfully involved in wildlife recovery by turning around the populations of certain animals.

NEW DELHI: The news of TMC chairperson Mamata Banerjee arriving in Delhi on Thursday evening has heightened the anticipation that an appointment sought by INDIA bloc for a meeting with President Droupadi Murmu over the functioning of Election Commission and the SIR process may be coming soon.Opposition INDIA bloc parties have agreed to restrict their delegation to 10 as sought by the President Secretariat, sources said.There was no confirmation from opposition parties as of Wednesday night if they have received an appointment from the President’s Secretariat. Article Title: India, Canada back CEPA with PM set to visit Ottawa on way to G20
Article Text:

The latest round of India-Canada security dialogue saw both sides welcoming efforts to advance negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), while underlining the growing potential for advancing a “substantive bilateral defence relationship in keeping with the vision of the leadership".The 2 sides are expected to sign the CEPA during PM Narendra Modi’s visit to Canada which, according to official sources, is tentatively scheduled for December 11-13. It will come days before the G20 summit for which Modi and Canadian PM Mark Carney will join President Donald Trump and other leaders in Florida. India and Canada are currently holding the 5th round of negotiations for CEPA. Both leaders have called for an ambitious and mutually beneficial CEPA that can serve as a durable anchor for the economic partnership, while allowing India and Canada to boost bilateral trade to CAD 70 billion (49 billion USD) by 2030.Both sides believe CEPA will be an apt culmination of the process of normalisation of ties, which started with Carney assuming office last year, amid the ongoing stalemate with the US over a trade deal . Efforts to ramp up defence cooperation could also lead to some significant outcomes during what will be Modi’s first bilateral visit to the country since the diplomatic row over the killing of a Khalistan separatist.Canada’s trade and foreign ministers, Maninder Sidhu and Anita Anand respectively, will also visit India this month.In a joint statement, NSA Ajit Doval and his counterpart David Morrison noted with satisfaction the sustained and constructive bilateral engagements over the past year, guided by mutual trust, respect for each other’s concerns and sensitivities, and a shared commitment to strengthening bilateral relations.“Both sides acknowledged the guidance provided by their respective Prime Ministers during their meetings in New Delhi in March 2026 and on the margins of the G7 Summit in Évian in June 2026,” said the joint statement, adding that Doval and Morrison reviewed progress in bilateral security and law enforcement cooperation, including the implementation of the shared Security Work Plan concluded in February 2026.They also reaffirmed their commitment to identifying additional areas for practical cooperation, including exploring the establishment of structured dialogues on cyber security and economic security.Both sides agreed to strengthen existing institutional mechanisms and establish new channels, to facilitate “streamlined communication” and timely information-sharing on matters of mutual concern.“They agreed to deepen coordination and cooperation in combating transnational organised crime, terrorism and violent extremism, human and drug trafficking, cybercrime, extortion, and extradition of criminal offenders,” said the statement.
Article Summary: The 2 sides are expected to sign the cepa during pm narendra modi’s visit to canada. It will come days before the g20 summit for which modi and canadian pm mark carney will join president donald trump. Both sides believe cepa will be an apt culmination of the process of normalisation of ties.

Article Title: Oceans connect, not divide nations, PM Modi says, calls for secure maritime order
Article Text:

Doubling down on India’s stand that sea lanes must not be turned into war zones and proposal to end conflict on Black Sea, PM Narendra Modi said oceans don’t separate countries but these connect them while calling for a free, open, secure and rules-based maritime order.In a message that was read out at Great Oceans Dialogue in Delhi, PM said, “The oceans do not separate us, they connect us, because what happens in one part of the world can have an impact far beyond its shores...Our vision is a free, open, secure and rule-based maritime that brings greater peace, prosperity and progress for all.” Modi said India’s maritime vision extends across regions and oceans, and is built on “cooperation, trust, mutual respect and mutual benefit”.His remarks come amid efforts to push a maritime understanding between Russia and Ukraine to keep the Black Sea open for commercial shipping and prevent attacks on vessels and critical maritime infrastructure. India’s three-part ceasefire plan seeks to halt attacks on energy facilities and other critical infrastructure; continuous and unhindered movement of grain, crude oil, LNG and LPG through Black Sea ports; and a complete stop to attacks on commercial vessels, merchant ships, and maritime operations to safeguard seafarers and global supply chains.The emphasis on maritime freedom assumes significance as attacks and disruptions in the Black Sea have affected commercial shipping, ports and movement of agricultural commodities during the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war.Participating in a panel discussion, Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan said that they don’t make any distinction between national security and national economic security. Swaminathan added that maritime security affects all nations as he stressed on the need for partnerships.The officer said that the vastness of oceans made cooperation, collaboration and resource-sharing is essential.He added all nations should maintain maritime domain awareness and share broad assessments of threats. Invoking PM’s SAGAR and MAHASAGAR formulations, Swaminathan said maritime threats are increasingly transregional because oceans are contiguous. Cooperation, therefore, must extend beyond individual regions, with regions working together for collective security and growth.
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi said oceans don’t separate countries but these connect them while calling for a free, open, secure and rules-based maritime order. His remarks come amid efforts to push a maritime understanding between russia and ukraine to keep the black sea open for commercial shipping.

NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday reiterated that it wants to keep neighbourly relations stable and cooperative, and that its diplomacy with Bangladesh rests on a positive, people-focused outlook geared towards shared growth and regional development.At a press briefing on bilateral ties and regional cooperation, foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that in high-level dialogues with Bangladeshi authorities, India continues to give priority to practical cooperation and joint economic progress, concentrating on initiatives that deliver direct benefits to the citizens of both countries."Our approach towards Bangladesh is to have positive, constructive, and forward-looking engagement with a people-centric focus for mutual growth and prosperity," Jaiswal stated. "We remain focused on this objective during our discussions with Bangladesh authorities."Earlier on Saturday, Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh, Dinesh Trivedi, said that former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's arrival in New Delhi two years ago was “unexpected”, adding that the Indian military had no part in arranging her extradition to India.Trivedi was speaking at the Bay of Bengal Conversation in Dhaka, an event hosted by a local think tank, the Centre for Governance Studies.He took questions on Hasina's legal status and the continuing debate over her extradition.Responding to those demands, Trivedi stated, "Hasinaji was not brought to India by the Indian Air Force or the Indian Army." He further noted, "It so happened because of the tragic circumstances in Bangladesh during that time. We hope and pray that should never happen, where innocent people get killed, doesn’t matter in which part of the world."The high commissioner said the development took Indian authorities by surprise."The military aircraft came to India… India was not prepared. I was watching on television, and the scroll was coming that she was going to some other country. At that point, Hasinaji was still the prime minister of Bangladesh. We had hardly any choice on that. It was our duty as a neighbour to accept the reality of life. Because situations are such that at times you are not prepared for such.""What was our [India’s] choice?" Trivedi asked, noting that refusing "landing permission" could have fundamentally changed how events unfolded. He added that both countries are vibrant democracies whose respective "legal systems" are actively examining matters relating to bilateral legal procedures.The interim administration of Bangladesh lodged its first formal extradition request in December 2024. Since then, the government of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, which took office after the February 2026 general elections, has repeatedly renewed the call.
Article Summary: India seeks 'positive, constructive, and forward-looking' engagement with bangladesh. India continues to give priority to practical cooperation and joint economic progress. NEW DELHI: India has fiercely condemned Pakistan for continuing to sponsor cross-border terrorism, declaring that televised media campaigns cannot alter the grim facts on the ground.Ministry of external affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal delivered the scathing rebuke during a press briefing in New Delhi on Wednesday. The statement follows a series of intense diplomatic clashes at the 81st United Nations general assembly (UNGA) and ongoing regional tensions."Pakistan is a country which has been fueling cross-border terrorism for years; lying and propagating falsehoods have become second nature to it," Jaiswal told reporters.New Delhi’s latest offensive targets what it calls Pakistan's ongoing public relations campaigns and media narratives. The MEA dismissed these broadcasts as an attempt to deflect international accountability and project a false image of peace."I want to emphasise that no matter how hard they try, the drama staged for television cannot alter the ground reality," Jaiswal added.The diplomatic row has escalated rapidly following sharp exchanges at the UNGA in New York.India recently exercised its Right of Reply at the UN to counter Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. Indian diplomats strongly rejected Sharif's statements, accusing Islamabad of using falsehoods and deceit to mislead the global community.Bilateral relations have remained severely strained since India launched Operation Sindoor. The retaliatory precision airstrikes targeted terrorist infrastructure across the Line of Control.With this latest statement, India has reaffirmed its rigid stance on regional security. New Delhi maintains that normal diplomatic engagement is impossible until Islamabad takes verifiable action to dismantle terror launchpads on its soil.

Russia has welcomed India’s readiness to make a “feasible contribution” towards resolving the Ukraine conflict. On Wednesday, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Moscow was grateful to New Delhi for its willingness to help and the ideas it has proposed.“Indeed, India is declaring readiness to make a feasible contribution to resolving the situation surrounding Ukraine,” Peskov said, according to state-run TASS, while responding to reports that India had sent a new three-part proposal for a peaceful resolution.“We are grateful to our Indian friends for such readiness and the ideas that are being offered,” he added.Peskov’s remarks come days after Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said India’s proposal for a possible ceasefire was the “broadest” among four offers received by Kyiv. The other proposals were from Turkiye, Egypt and the US.“We have four proposals. The broadest one is India’s proposal. We are ready for an energy and Black Sea ceasefire, but only in this combination,” Sybiha told reporters in Kyiv on Friday, according to European Pravda.India’s efforts have also received praise from Russian president Vladimir Putin.Ahead of the BRICS summit in New Delhi last month, Putin and Modi held talks during which the Russian leader briefed the Prime Minister on the Ukraine conflict and ongoing peace initiatives.On Friday, Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had “good ideas” aimed at finding mutually acceptable solutions to the conflict.“Prime Minister Narendra Modi is one of those world leaders who, despite our very good and even friendly relations, personal good relations, constantly raises the question and asks the question about putting an end to the conflict in Ukraine,” Putin said.“He has an avid interest and very good ideas aimed at finding mutually acceptable solutions. In that sense, naturally, the Prime Minister takes a neutral position but with an interest in the end of the conflict,” he added.Putin also said, “I think it’s my duty to say that directly. And we are thankful to the Prime Minister for his ideas.”Modi has repeatedly maintained that India is willing to support meaningful efforts towards peace. Responding to a question on India’s role, he said, “I have already indicated India’s willingness to support meaningful efforts aimed at achieving a peaceful resolution of the conflict.”External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said on Sunday that India had moved beyond advocacy and intensified engagement with both Kyiv and Moscow. He said New Delhi was focusing on issues including the safety of shipping in the Black Sea, grain exports and energy supplies.India has consistently advocated dialogue and diplomacy to resolve the conflict, now in its fifth year. Ukraine, meanwhile, has called for an unconditional ceasefire, including an end to attacks on energy and port infrastructure and a halt to hostilities in the Black Sea.
Article Summary: Russia has welcomed india’s readiness to make a “feasible contribution” towards resolving the ukraine conflict. On wednesday, kremlin spokesperson dmitry peskov said moscow was grateful to new delhi for its willingness to help. On friday, putin said prime minister narendra modi had “good ideas” aimed at finding mutually acceptable solutions.

Article Title: Meta claims it acted on 5.3 million child abuse content in India, over 98% found proactively

NEW DELHI: Meta on Wednesday said it has taken action against 5.3 million pieces of child sexual exploitation content on Facebook and Instagram in India between January and June 2026, with more than 98 per cent detected proactively, the company told news agency PTI.Meta also said it had introduced additional measures to strengthen efforts to combat child sexual exploitation on its platforms.The latest disclosure comes after the government had told Meta that it could not continue to invoke its intermediary status and needed to take greater responsibility for child sexual abuse material on its platforms.The government had warned that Meta could risk losing the “safe harbour” immunity available to intermediaries if it failed to meet its obligations. Officials had also pointed to the company’s recommendation and advertising systems, saying they gave Meta responsibilities beyond merely hosting users’ posts.Meta had admitted to lapses in dealing with child sexual abuse material and assured authorities that it would immediately report such content, according to people familiar with the matter.The government had also made it clear that Meta needed to remove child sexual abuse material that could drive children to suicide.The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) had separately warned Meta representatives when Meta India chief Arun Srinivas and senior executives appeared before the panel as part of its inquiry into alleged advertisements linked to child sexual exploitation and abuse material on the platform.Against this backdrop, Meta on Wednesday said it had introduced additional measures to strengthen efforts to combat child sexual exploitation on its platforms.

NEW DELHI: Captain Smit Machchhar, the Indian pilot injured in a mid-air attack on a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight, is “recuperating well” and responding positively to treatment, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Tuesday.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Machchhar remains hospitalised in Abu Dhabi, with the Indian embassy in the UAE maintaining regular contact with him, his family and local authorities.“Captain Smit Machchhar is in the hospital in Abu Dhabi. Our embassy in the UAE has been in regular touch with him, with his family, with local authorities, and with the hospital authorities. He's recuperating well. He's responding well. And his health is improving,” Jaiswal said.The update came after the Indian Embassy in the UAE said Machchhar was making “steady progress” and “regaining his health”. The pilot suffered severe injuries to his head, neck and hand after co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national, attacked him during the flight and attempted to take control of the aircraft.Machchhar's condition had become critical during the incident, with heavy bleeding from his injuries and his pulse dropping dangerously low.He was kept stable during the flight by Dr Shuta Musaev, a Georgian dentist living in Israel who was the only doctor on board.Musaev told ABC News that he used T-shirts as pressure dressings and ice packs to control the bleeding for around 45 minutes. At one point, Machchhar's pulse became dangerously low and Musaev raised his feet until his pulse recovered.“When I saw his lips were blue, I told the steward, 'We need to land quickly. He doesn’t have much more time',” Musaev said.Machchhar was eventually handed over to medical teams after the aircraft landed in Saudi Arabia. He has since been receiving treatment in the UAE.The pilot has been hailed as a “hero” by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for his actions during the attack. Musaev also credited Machchhar with helping save the lives of those on board.
Article Summary: Captain smit machchhar is “recuperating well” and responding positively to treatment, the ministry of external affairs said. The pilot suffered severe injuries to his head, neck and hand after co-pilot hamam al-hammami, an omani national, attacked him during the flight.
